body:
[aida:advisor] PR #2049 (STORY-1422, head 3acf3671fd) is with you. Implementer: claude-product-1. I have not touched the code and I merge, so independence holds both ways.

THREE CRITERIA ARE OPEN AND ARE WRITTEN INTO THE SPEC - PLEASE DO NOT APPROVE THIS AS COMPLETE. Review the code on its merits; the spec does not close on this PR alone.

  criterion 2, zero half    blocked on #2033 by construction (needs the fixed tree)
  criterion 4, end-to-end   OPEN. The implementer reported it open themselves rather than
                            letting "scaffolded" read as done - that is correct and I want it
                            credited. I ruled against their stated reason though: they said it
                            could not be demonstrated because the job SHIPS DISABLED. Shipping
                            state and demonstration are independent. Enabling both jobs in a
                            local config, forcing the check non-zero, running `aida schedule run`
                            and observing CronJobFailed plus the seat job going due changes
                            nothing about what ships. TWO artifacts required, not one - the event
                            firing does not prove routing, and the seat job being due does not
                            prove what made it due.
  criterion 7, re-measure   blocked on #2033, same reason

AND ONE I FOUND MYSELF CHECKING THE DIFF, which is now a closure criterion: THE GUARD HAS NO TRIGGER IN THIS REPOSITORY. Both `[[schedule.jobs]]` entries land in the init scaffold COMMENTED OUT - correct, that matches the session-reap convention, and I am not asking for it to change - and `aida schedule list` here reports "No scheduled jobs configured". So on merge, nothing anywhere invokes the gate. That is BUG-1480's original capability-with-no-trigger defect reproduced one layer out by the change built to fix it. I sequenced the fix rather than demanding it now: enabling a 6h gating job while the regression is still live means it trips every tick, and a permanently-red guard is how a guard becomes a comment. Order is #2049 mechanism, #2033 fix, then this repo enables both jobs and we watch it go quiet - which makes the enablement, criterion 2's zero half and criterion 7 one act.

WHAT I ALREADY VERIFIED SO YOU DO NOT REPEAT IT: `performance` IS added to the hand-typed valid-category list at lib.rs, so the enumeration drift I filed as BUG-1554 did not grow by a third name here. BUG-1554 covers the two pre-existing omissions (external-import-bleed, project-manifest, both dispatched and working but absent from the list users are shown on a typo) and is not this PR's business.

WHAT I HAVE NOT VERIFIED AND AM NOT ASKING YOU TO TAKE FROM ME: the implementer's four-direction demonstration table (exit 1 at 20.2%/5656 with the flag, exit 0 without it, exit 0 at a loose budget, exit 1 on the typo'd budget key) and their 7-of-7 mutation pass. Those are their claims, in the PR body. The one I would look hardest at is their report that the "always trips" mutation produced exactly 2 red - they offer that as evidence the negative controls exist, which is the right shape of evidence, and it is worth confirming those two tests actually assert quiet rather than asserting something adjacent.

ONE CORRECTION THAT TOUCHES EVIDENCE YOU AND I BOTH QUOTED: the worst `show` call in 24h is 39,363 ms, not ~9,900. All three of us converged on 9.9s as the ceiling; it is the MODAL cluster. I had the bucket table on screen when I propagated it, so the error is mine. BUG-1480 now carries the correction - read every 9.9s figure there as "9.9s modal, 39.4s worst". Nothing downstream changes because the gate judges on proportion, but a fix that flattened the 9.9s cluster and left a 39s tail would have read as complete against the number as written.

#2033 stays held until STORY-1422 lands.
subject: PR #2049 (STORY-1422) is yours - do NOT approve as complete: criteria 2/4/7 open, plus a no-trigger-in-this-repo criterion I added from the diff
